extends Node2D

# Tunables
var PLAYER_SPEED = 240.0
var JELLYFISH_FLEE_SPEED = 80.0      # slow, as intensity 3/10
var GOAL_RADIUS = 80.0               # wide pool entrance
var SURVIVAL_TIME = 90.0             # generous time for level 1
var ROCK_SIZE = Vector2(128, 128)
var MAX_JELLYFISH = 3

# State
var state = "title"
var time_left = SURVIVAL_TIME
var jellyfish_inside = []            # nodes currently inside the goal

# Nodes
var player: Area2D
var goal: Area2D
var jellyfishes = []                 # all jellyfish Area2D nodes
var rock_rects = []                  # Rect2 for each obstacle
var status_label: Label
var win_called = false

func _ready():
    # Background
    var bg = Sprite2D.new()
    bg.texture = load("res://assets/level_0_bg_00019_.png")
    bg.centered = false
    bg.position = Vector2.ZERO
    bg.z_index = -1
    add_child(bg)

    # -- Rocks (obstacles) --
    _add_rock(Vector2(600, 400))
    _add_rock(Vector2(300, 350))
    _add_rock(Vector2(750, 200))

    # -- Player --
    player = Area2D.new()
    player.position = Vector2(200, 500)
    var player_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
    player_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/hero_sprite_00019_.png")
    player.add_child(player_sprite)
    var player_col = CollisionShape2D.new()
    var player_circle = CircleShape2D.new()
    player_circle.radius = 30.0
    player_col.shape = player_circle
    player.add_child(player_col)
    add_child(player)

    # -- Jellyfish (creatures) --
    var jstart = [Vector2(150, 200), Vector2(300, 150), Vector2(100, 400)]
    for i in jstart.size():
        var j = Area2D.new()
        j.position = jstart[i]
        var jsprite = Sprite2D.new()
        jsprite.texture = load("res://assets/key_item_00016_.png")
        j.add_child(jsprite)
        var jcol = CollisionShape2D.new()
        var jcircle = CircleShape2D.new()
        jcircle.radius = 20.0
        jcol.shape = jcircle
        j.add_child(jcol)
        j.add_to_group("jellyfish")
        jellyfishes.append(j)
        add_child(j)

    # -- Goal zone (tide pool) --
    goal = Area2D.new()
    goal.position = Vector2(800, 500)
    var goal_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
    goal_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_tide_pool_00001_.png")
    goal_sprite.scale = Vector2(1.5, 1.5)   # visually wider
    goal.add_child(goal_sprite)
    var goal_col = CollisionShape2D.new()
    var goal_circle = CircleShape2D.new()
    goal_circle.radius = GOAL_RADIUS
    goal_col.shape = goal_circle
    goal.add_child(goal_col)
    goal.area_entered.connect(_on_goal_entered)
    goal.area_exited.connect(_on_goal_exited)
    add_child(goal)

    # -- UI --
    var canvas = CanvasLayer.new()
    add_child(canvas)
    status_label = Label.new()
    status_label.position = Vector2(20, 20)
    status_label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 24)
    canvas.add_child(status_label)

    # Auto-start for headless or non-first level
    if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless" or Game.level > 0:
        state = "playing"

func _add_rock(pos: Vector2):
    var rock = Area2D.new()
    rock.position = pos
    var sprite = Sprite2D.new()
    sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_rock_00001_.png")
    rock.add_child(sprite)
    var col = CollisionShape2D.new()
    var rect_shape = RectangleShape2D.new()
    rect_shape.size = ROCK_SIZE
    col.shape = rect_shape
    rock.add_child(col)
    add_child(rock)
    # Store physical rect for manual collision checks
    rock_rects.append(Rect2(pos - ROCK_SIZE/2, ROCK_SIZE))

func _process(delta):
    if state == "title":
        status_label.text = "BLINDSIGHT BEACH\nMoonlit Sands\nPress Enter to start"
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            state = "playing"
        return

    if state == "won":
        return

    if state == "over":
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            get_tree().reload_current_scene()
        return

    # Playing state
    # Timer
    time_left -= delta
    if time_left <= 0.0:
        state = "over"
        Sfx.play("lose")
        status_label.text = "The sun has risen...\nJellyfish stranded.\nPress Enter to restart"
        return

    # Player input
    var velocity = Vector2.ZERO
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"): velocity.x += 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):  velocity.x -= 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):  velocity.y += 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):    velocity.y -= 1.0
    velocity = velocity.normalized() * PLAYER_SPEED * delta

    # Player collision with rocks (slide along edges)
    var new_pos = player.position + velocity
    for rock in rock_rects:
        if rock.has_point(Vector2(new_pos.x, player.position.y)):
            new_pos.x = player.position.x
        if rock.has_point(Vector2(player.position.x, new_pos.y)):
            new_pos.y = player.position.y
    new_pos = new_pos.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
    player.position = new_pos

    # Jellyfish movement (flee) + rock collision
    for j in jellyfishes:
        var direction = (j.position - player.position).normalized()
        var move = direction * JELLYFISH_FLEE_SPEED * delta
        var npos = j.position + move

        # Slide along rocks
        for rock in rock_rects:
            if rock.has_point(Vector2(npos.x, j.position.y)):
                npos.x = j.position.x
            if rock.has_point(Vector2(j.position.x, npos.y)):
                npos.y = j.position.y

        npos = npos.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
        j.position = npos

    # UI text
    status_label.text = "Jellyfish in pool: %d/%d   Sunrise in: %ds" % [jellyfish_inside.size(), MAX_JELLYFISH, int(ceil(time_left))]

func _on_goal_entered(area: Area2D):
    if area.is_in_group("jellyfish") and area not in jellyfish_inside:
        jellyfish_inside.append(area)
        _check_win()

func _on_goal_exited(area: Area2D):
    if area.is_in_group("jellyfish") and area in jellyfish_inside:
        jellyfish_inside.erase(area)

func _check_win():
    if state == "playing" and jellyfish_inside.size() == MAX_JELLYFISH:
        state = "won"
        Sfx.play("win")
        status_label.text = "All jellyfish safe!\nLevel complete."
        if not win_called:
            win_called = true
            Game.level_complete()

extends Node2D

# tuning variables (scaled for level 6/10 intensity)
var player_speed = 300.0
var flee_speed = 325.0   # increased from ~250 base
var goal_zone_radius = 18.0   # shrunken hitbox for goal
var survival_time = 30.0
var player_collision_radius = 20.0
var jelly_collision_radius = 20.0
var rock_extents = Vector2(64, 64)

var total_jellyfish = 3
var rescued = 0
var time_left

var state = "title"

var player: Area2D
var status_label: Label
var rocks = []
var jellyfish = []
var tide_pools = []

func _ready():
	# background
	var bg = Sprite2D.new()
	bg.texture = load("res://assets/level_1_bg_00015_.png")
	bg.centered = false
	bg.position = Vector2.ZERO
	bg.z_index = -1
	add_child(bg)

	# player
	player = Area2D.new()
	player.position = Vector2(200, 300)
	var player_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	player_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/hero_sprite_00019_.png")
	player.add_child(player_sprite)
	var player_shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
	var circle = CircleShape2D.new()
	circle.radius = player_collision_radius
	player_shape.shape = circle
	player.add_child(player_shape)
	# no signal needed for player - only used for rock overlap detection
	add_child(player)

	# jellyfish (creatures)
	var jelly_starts = [Vector2(750, 150), Vector2(350, 480), Vector2(550, 100)]
	for pos in jelly_starts:
		var jelly = Area2D.new()
		jelly.position = pos
		jelly.add_to_group("jellyfish")
		var jelly_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
		jelly_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/key_item_00016_.png")
		jelly.add_child(jelly_sprite)
		var jshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
		var jcircle = CircleShape2D.new()
		jcircle.radius = jelly_collision_radius
		jshape.shape = jcircle
		jelly.add_child(jshape)
		add_child(jelly)
		jellyfish.append(jelly)

	# tide pools (goal zones)
	var pool_positions = [Vector2(150, 150), Vector2(800, 400), Vector2(500, 200)]
	for pos in pool_positions:
		var pool = Area2D.new()
		pool.position = pos
		var pool_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
		pool_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_tide_pool_00001_.png")
		pool.add_child(pool_sprite)
		var pshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
		var pcircle = CircleShape2D.new()
		pcircle.radius = goal_zone_radius
		pshape.shape = pcircle
		pool.add_child(pshape)
		pool.area_entered.connect(_on_tide_pool_entered)
		add_child(pool)
		tide_pools.append(pool)

	# rocks (obstacles)
	var rock_positions = [Vector2(400, 100), Vector2(700, 250), Vector2(300, 400)]
	for pos in rock_positions:
		var rock = Area2D.new()
		rock.position = pos
		var rock_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
		rock_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_rock_00001_.png")
		rock.add_child(rock_sprite)
		var rshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
		var rect = RectangleShape2D.new()
		rect.extents = rock_extents
		rshape.shape = rect
		rock.add_child(rshape)
		add_child(rock)
		rocks.append(rock)

	# UI
	var canvas = CanvasLayer.new()
	add_child(canvas)
	status_label = Label.new()
	status_label.position = Vector2(20, 20)
	status_label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 20)
	canvas.add_child(status_label)

	time_left = survival_time

	# skip title for levels beyond first or headless
	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless" or Game.level > 0:
		state = "playing"

func _on_tide_pool_entered(area: Area2D):
	if state != "playing":
		return
	if area.is_in_group("jellyfish"):
		area.queue_free()
		jellyfish.erase(area)
		rescued += 1
		Sfx.play("pickup")
		if rescued >= total_jellyfish:
			state = "won"
			Sfx.play("win")
			status_label.text = "All jellyfish returned to the sea - level complete!"
			Game.level_complete()

func _process(delta):
	if state == "title":
		status_label.text = "BLINDSIGHT BEACH - Press Enter to start"
		if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
			state = "playing"
		return
	if state == "won":
		return
	if state == "over":
		if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
			get_tree().reload_current_scene()
		return

	# timer
	time_left -= delta
	if time_left <= 0.0 and rescued < total_jellyfish:
		state = "over"
		Sfx.play("lose")
		status_label.text = "The sun has baked the remaining jellyfish...  Press Enter to restart"
		return

	# player movement
	var input_dir = Vector2.ZERO
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"):
		input_dir.x += 1.0
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
		input_dir.x -= 1.0
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):
		input_dir.y += 1.0
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
		input_dir.y -= 1.0

	var vel = input_dir.normalized() * player_speed
	player.position += vel * delta

	# rock collision (push-out)
	for rock in rocks:
		var min_corner = rock.position - rock_extents
		var max_corner = rock.position + rock_extents
		var closest = Vector2(
			clamp(player.position.x, min_corner.x, max_corner.x),
			clamp(player.position.y, min_corner.y, max_corner.y)
		)
		if player.position.distance_to(closest) < player_collision_radius:
			var dir = player.position - closest
			player.position = closest + dir.normalized() * player_collision_radius

	# clamp to viewport
	player.position = player.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))

	# jellyfish flee behaviour
	for jelly in jellyfish:
		var to_player = jelly.position - player.position
		if to_player.length() > 0.1:
			var flee_dir = to_player.normalized()
			jelly.position += flee_dir * flee_speed * delta
		jelly.position = jelly.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))

	# status display
	status_label.text = "Sunrise in " + str(int(ceil(time_left))) + "s   Rescued: " + str(rescued) + "/" + str(total_jellyfish)

extends Node2D

# Configuration
const PLAYER_SPEED = 240.0
const JELLYFISH_FLEE_SPEED = 400.0
const ROCK_RADIUS = 64.0
const ROCK_AVOID_DIST = 80.0
const ROCK_REPULSION_STRENGTH = 400.0
const GOAL_SCALE = 0.5
const GOAL_RADIUS = 32.0
const SURVIVAL_TIME = 45.0
const TOTAL_JELLYFISH = 3

var state = "title"
var player: Area2D
var jellyfish_list = []
var rocks = []
var goal: Area2D
var collected = 0
var time_left = SURVIVAL_TIME
var label: Label

func _ready():
	# Background
	var bg = Sprite2D.new()
	bg.texture = load("res://assets/level_2_bg_00014_.png")
	bg.centered = false
	bg.position = Vector2.ZERO
	bg.z_index = -1
	add_child(bg)

	# Rocks
	var rock_positions = [
		Vector2(200, 200), Vector2(300, 300), Vector2(500, 400),
		Vector2(700, 200), Vector2(800, 400), Vector2(400, 200),
		Vector2(600, 100), Vector2(300, 100)
	]
	for pos in rock_positions:
		var rock = Node2D.new()
		rock.position = pos
		var sprite = Sprite2D.new()
		sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_rock_00001_.png")
		sprite.centered = true
		rock.add_child(sprite)
		add_child(rock)
		rocks.append(rock)

	# Goal
	goal = Area2D.new()
	goal.position = Vector2(900, 500)
	var goal_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	goal_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_tide_pool_00001_.png")
	goal_sprite.centered = true
	goal_sprite.scale = Vector2(GOAL_SCALE, GOAL_SCALE)
	goal.add_child(goal_sprite)
	var goal_shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
	goal_shape.shape = CircleShape2D.new()
	goal_shape.shape.radius = GOAL_RADIUS
	goal.add_child(goal_shape)
	goal.area_entered.connect(_on_goal_entered)
	add_child(goal)

	# Player
	player = Area2D.new()
	player.position = Vector2(80, 500)
	var cat_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	cat_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/hero_sprite_00019_.png")
	cat_sprite.centered = true
	player.add_child(cat_sprite)
	var player_shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
	player_shape.shape = CircleShape2D.new()
	player_shape.shape.radius = 20.0
	player.add_child(player_shape)
	add_child(player)

	# Jellyfish
	var jelly_spawns = [Vector2(150, 100), Vector2(850, 100), Vector2(400, 50)]
	for pos in jelly_spawns:
		var j = Area2D.new()
		j.position = pos
		var jsprite = Sprite2D.new()
		jsprite.texture = load("res://assets/key_item_00016_.png")
		jsprite.centered = true
		j.add_child(jsprite)
		var jshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
		jshape.shape = CircleShape2D.new()
		jshape.shape.radius = 20.0
		j.add_child(jshape)
		add_child(j)
		jellyfish_list.append(j)

	# UI
	var canvas = CanvasLayer.new()
	add_child(canvas)
	label = Label.new()
	label.position = Vector2(20, 20)
	canvas.add_child(label)

	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless" or Game.level > 0:
		state = "playing"

func _on_goal_entered(area: Area2D):
	if state != "playing":
		return
	for j in jellyfish_list:
		if j == area:
			jellyfish_list.erase(j)
			j.queue_free()
			collected += 1
			Sfx.play("pickup")
			if collected >= TOTAL_JELLYFISH:
				state = "won"
				Sfx.play("win")
				label.text = "All jellyfish reach the sea! Dawn is safe."
				Game.level_complete()
			break

func _process(delta):
	if state == "title":
		label.text = "BLINDSIGHT BEACH\nPress Enter to start"
		if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
			state = "playing"
		return
	if state == "won":
		return
	if state == "over":
		label.text = "The sun has risen... Press Enter to restart"
		if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
			get_tree().reload_current_scene()
		return

	# Timer
	time_left -= delta
	if time_left <= 0.0 and collected < TOTAL_JELLYFISH:
		state = "over"
		Sfx.play("lose")
		label.text = "The sun rises before all are safe. Press Enter to restart"
		return

	# Player movement
	var vel = Vector2.ZERO
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"):
		vel.x += 1.0
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
		vel.x -= 1.0
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):
		vel.y += 1.0
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
		vel.y -= 1.0
	var new_pos = player.position + vel.normalized() * PLAYER_SPEED * delta
	for rock in rocks:
		var to_rock = new_pos - rock.position
		if to_rock.length() < ROCK_RADIUS:
			new_pos = rock.position + to_rock.normalized() * ROCK_RADIUS
	player.position = new_pos.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))

	# Jellyfish movement
	for j in jellyfish_list:
		var to_player = player.position - j.position
		var flee_dir = -to_player.normalized() if to_player.length() > 0.01 else Vector2.ZERO
		var vel_j = flee_dir * JELLYFISH_FLEE_SPEED
		# Avoid rocks
		for rock in rocks:
			var to_rock = j.position - rock.position
			var dist = to_rock.length()
			if dist < ROCK_AVOID_DIST:
				var repulsion = to_rock.normalized() * ROCK_REPULSION_STRENGTH * (1.0 - dist / ROCK_AVOID_DIST)
				vel_j += repulsion

		j.position = new_jpos

extends Node2D

# Tuning variables (intensity 3/10 - easy, first level)
var player_speed = 240.0
var flee_speed = 60.0          # well below 60% of player speed (144)
var panic_radius = 120.0       # small panic radius, easier herding
var sunrise_time = 60.0        # generous time limit
var jellyfish_count = 4        # fewer creatures than a harder level
var goal_scale = 2.0           # makes the tide pool entrance wide
var rock_count = 4

# Runtime state
var state = "title"
var time_left = sunrise_time
var settled_count = 0
var jellyfish_nodes = []
var rock_nodes = []
var goal_area: Area2D
var player: Area2D
var status_label: Label

func _ready():
    # Background
    var bg = Sprite2D.new()
    bg.texture = load("res://assets/level_0_bg_00001_.png")
    bg.centered = false
    bg.position = Vector2.ZERO
    bg.z_index = -1
    add_child(bg)

    # Player (the blind cat)
    player = Area2D.new()
    player.position = Vector2(200, 288)
    var psprite = Sprite2D.new()
    psprite.texture = load("res://assets/hero_sprite_00001_.png")
    player.add_child(psprite)
    var pshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
    var pcircle = CircleShape2D.new()
    pcircle.radius = 20.0
    pshape.shape = pcircle
    player.add_child(pshape)
    add_child(player)

    # Rocks (obstacles)
    var rock_positions = [Vector2(300, 250), Vector2(500, 150), Vector2(700, 450), Vector2(200, 100)]
    for pos in rock_positions:
        var rock = Area2D.new()
        rock.position = pos
        var rsprite = Sprite2D.new()
        rsprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_rock_00001_.png")
        rock.add_child(rsprite)
        var rshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
        var rrect = RectangleShape2D.new()
        rrect.size = Vector2(128, 128)  # matches sprite size
        rshape.shape = rrect
        rock.add_child(rshape)
        add_child(rock)
        rock_nodes.append(rock)

    # Goal zone (tide pool) - wide, placed on the right side
    goal_area = Area2D.new()
    goal_area.position = Vector2(750, 300)
    var gsprite = Sprite2D.new()
    gsprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_tide_pool_00001_.png")
    gsprite.scale = Vector2(goal_scale, goal_scale)  # visually larger
    goal_area.add_child(gsprite)
    var gshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
    var grect = RectangleShape2D.new()
    grect.size = Vector2(128 * goal_scale, 128 * goal_scale)
    gshape.shape = grect
    goal_area.add_child(gshape)
    add_child(goal_area)
    goal_area.area_entered.connect(_on_goal_area_entered)

    # Jellyfish (creatures)
    var jelly_positions = [Vector2(300, 400), Vector2(500, 450), Vector2(650, 200), Vector2(400, 150)]
    for i in jellyfish_count:
        var jelly = Area2D.new()
        jelly.position = jelly_positions[i]
        var jsprite = Sprite2D.new()
        jsprite.texture = load("res://assets/key_item_00001_.png")
        jelly.add_child(jsprite)
        var jshape = CollisionShape2D.new()
        var jcircle = CircleShape2D.new()
        jcircle.radius = 16.0
        jshape.shape = jcircle
        jelly.add_child(jshape)
        jelly.set_meta("settled", false)
        add_child(jelly)
        jellyfish_nodes.append(jelly)

    # UI label
    var canvas = CanvasLayer.new()
    add_child(canvas)
    status_label = Label.new()
    status_label.position = Vector2(20, 20)
    canvas.add_child(status_label)

    # Auto-start in headless or later levels
    if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless" or Game.level > 0:
        state = "playing"

func _on_goal_area_entered(area: Area2D):
    if state != "playing":
        return
    if area in jellyfish_nodes and not area.get_meta("settled"):
        area.set_meta("settled", true)
        settled_count += 1
        Sfx.play("pickup")
        if settled_count >= jellyfish_count:
            state = "won"
            Sfx.play("win")
            status_label.text = "Tide pools full - level complete!"
            Game.level_complete()

func _is_overlapping_any_rock(area: Area2D) -> bool:
    for rock in rock_nodes:
        if area.overlaps_area(rock):
            return true
    return false

func _process(delta):
    if state == "title":
        status_label.text = "BLINDSIGHT BEACH - Moonlit Sands - Press Enter"
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            state = "playing"
            time_left = sunrise_time
        return

    if state == "won":
        return

    if state == "over":
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            get_tree().reload_current_scene()
        return

    # Playing state
    time_left -= delta
    if time_left <= 0.0:
        state = "over"
        Sfx.play("lose")
        status_label.text = "The sun rises... jellyfish lost. Press Enter to retry"
        return

    # Player movement
    var vel = Vector2.ZERO
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"):
        vel.x += 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
        vel.x -= 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):
        vel.y += 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
        vel.y -= 1.0

    var prev_player_pos = player.position
    if vel.length_squared() > 0.0:
        player.position += vel.normalized() * player_speed * delta
        player.position = player.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
        if _is_overlapping_any_rock(player):
            player.position = prev_player_pos

    # Jellyfish fleeing
    for jelly in jellyfish_nodes:
        if jelly.get_meta("settled"):
            continue
        var dist = player.position.distance_to(jelly.position)
        if dist < panic_radius and dist > 0.001:
            var dir = (jelly.position - player.position).normalized()
            var prev_jelly_pos = jelly.position
            jelly.position += dir * flee_speed * delta
            jelly.position = jelly.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
            if _is_overlapping_any_rock(jelly):
                jelly.position = prev_jelly_pos

    # UI update
    status_label.text = "Jellyfish: %d/%d  Sunrise in: %d s" % [settled_count, jellyfish_count, int(ceil(time_left))]

func _process(delta):
    if state == "title":
        status_label.text = "BLINDSIGHT BEACH\nPress Enter to start"

    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):

func _on_jellyfish_entered_goal(area: Area2D, jelly_data):
    if area == tide_pool_area and not jelly_data["settled"]:
        jelly_data["settled"] = true
        settled_count += 1

        if settled_count >= jellyfish_count:

func _process(delta):

            state = "playing"
        return
    if state == "won":
        return
    if state == "over":
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            get_tree().reload_current_scene()
        return

    # Timer
    time_left -= delta
    if time_left <= 0.0:
        if settled_count < jellyfish_count:
            state = "over"
            Sfx.play("lose")
            status_label.text = "The sun has risen...  Press Enter to restart"
        else:
            # already settled, but safety
            state = "won"
            Sfx.play("win")
            status_label.text = "Tide pool full - level complete!"
            Game.level_complete()
        return

    # Player movement
    var move_vec = Vector2.ZERO
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"): move_vec.x += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):  move_vec.x -= 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):  move_vec.y += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):    move_vec.y -= 1
    if move_vec.length() > 0:
        move_vec = move_vec.normalized()
    var new_player_pos = player.position + move_vec * player_speed * delta
    new_player_pos = new_player_pos.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
    player.position = _slide_against_rocks(player.position, new_player_pos)

    # Jellyfish panic/flee
    for jdata in jellyfish_list:
        if jdata["settled"]:
            continue
        var jelly = jdata["area"]
        var to_player = player.position - jelly.position
        if to_player.length() <= panic_radius:
            var flee_dir = (jelly.position - player.position).normalized()
            var target_pos = jelly.position + flee_dir * flee_speed * delta
            target_pos = target_pos.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
            jelly.position = _slide_against_rocks(jelly.position, target_pos)

    # Update status
    status_label.text = "Jellyfish: %d/%d | Time: %ds" % [settled_count, jellyfish_count, int(ceil(time_left))]

func _slide_against_rocks(from: Vector2, to: Vector2) -> Vector2:
    var best = to
    if not _rock_collides(to):
        return to
    # Try x-only
    var x_only = Vector2(to.x, from.y)
    if not _rock_collides(x_only):
        return x_only
    # Try y-only
    var y_only = Vector2(from.x, to.y)
    if not _rock_collides(y_only):
        return y_only
    # Block
    return from

func _rock_collides(point: Vector2) -> bool:
    for r in rock_rects:
        if r.has_point(point):
            return true
    return false

# Gameplay tuning – scale for Level 2 (intensity 6/10)
const PLAYER_SPEED = 240.0
const FLEE_SPEED = 80.0          # well below 60% of player speed
const PANIC_RADIUS = 130.0       # creatures bolt sooner
const SUNRISE_DURATION = 40.0    # shorter window to herd
const CREATURE_COUNT = 4         # more jellyfish
const GOAL_ZONE_SIZE = 128       # tide pool is 128x128
const VIEWPORT_W = 1024
const VIEWPORT_H = 576

var state = "title"
var time_left = SUNRISE_DURATION
var player: Area2D
var goal_zone: Area2D
var creatures: Array[Area2D] = []   # all jellyfish Area2Ds
var settled_count = 0
var status_label: Label

func _ready():
    # Background
    var bg = Sprite2D.new()
    bg.texture = load("res://assets/level_1_bg_00015_.png")

    bg.position = Vector2.ZERO
    bg.z_index = -1

    for pos in rock_positions:
        var rock = Sprite2D.new()

        add_child(rock)

    # Player

    player.position = Vector2(512, 288)
    var player_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
    player_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/hero_sprite_00019_.png")
    player.add_child(player_sprite)
    var player_shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
    player_shape.shape = CircleShape2D.new()

    # Panic zone – makes creatures flee when player is near
    var panic_zone = Area2D.new()

    panic_zone.area_entered.connect(_on_panic_entered)
    panic_zone.area_exited.connect(_on_panic_exited)
    player.add_child(panic_zone)
    add_child(player)

    # Goal zone – the tide pool
    goal_zone = Area2D.new()
    goal_zone.position = Vector2(200, 400)   # target area on the left side
    var zone_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
    zone_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_tide_pool_00001_.png")

    goal_zone.add_child(zone_shape)
    goal_zone.area_entered.connect(_on_goal_zone_entered)
    add_child(goal_zone)

    # Creatures (jellyfish)
    var start_positions = [
        Vector2(700, 200),
        Vector2(750, 250),
        Vector2(800, 300),
        Vector2(780, 150)
    ]
    for pos in start_positions:
        var creature = Area2D.new()
        creature.position = pos
        var sprite = Sprite2D.new()
        sprite.texture = load("res://assets/key_item_00016_.png")
        creature.add_child(sprite)
        var shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
        shape.shape = CircleShape2D.new()
        shape.shape.radius = 14.0
        creature.add_child(shape)

        creature.set_meta("is_creature", true)
        creature.set_meta("settled", false)

    # UI
    var canvas = CanvasLayer.new()

    status_label = Label.new()

func _on_goal_zone_entered(area: Area2D):
    if state != "playing":
        return
    if not area.has_meta("is_creature") or area.get_meta("settled"):
        return
    # Settle this jellyfish
    area.set_meta("settled", true)
    area.position = goal_zone.position
    settled_count += 1
    Sfx.play("pickup")
    if settled_count >= CREATURE_COUNT:
        _win()

func _on_panic_entered(area: Area2D):
    if area == player:
        return
    if area.has_meta("is_creature") and not area.get_meta("settled"):
        area.set_meta("panicked", true)

func _on_panic_exited(area: Area2D):
    if area == player:
        return
    if area.has_meta("is_creature"):
        area.set_meta("panicked", false)

func _process(delta):
    if state == "title":
        status_label.text = "Blindsight Beach - Press Enter to start"
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            state = "playing"
        return

        if state == "over" and Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            get_tree().reload_current_scene()
        return

    # Countdown
    time_left -= delta
    if time_left <= 0.0:
        if settled_count < CREATURE_COUNT:
            _lose()
            return
        else:
            _win()
            return

    # Player movement
    var velocity = Vector2.ZERO
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"): velocity.x += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):  velocity.x -= 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):  velocity.y += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):    velocity.y -= 1
    if velocity.length_squared() > 0:
        velocity = velocity.normalized() * PLAYER_SPEED
    player.position += velocity * delta
    player.position = player.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(VIEWPORT_W, VIEWPORT_H))

    # Creature movement – flee only when panicked
    for creature in creatures:
        if creature.get_meta("settled"):
            continue
        if not creature.get_meta("panicked", false):
            continue
        var flee_dir = creature.position - player.position
        if flee_dir.length_squared() > 0:
            flee_dir = flee_dir.normalized()
        creature.position += flee_dir * FLEE_SPEED * delta
        creature.position = creature.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(VIEWPORT_W, VIEWPORT_H))

    status_label.text = "Time: %ds  Saved: %d/%d" % [ceil(time_left), settled_count, CREATURE_COUNT]

func _win():
    state = "won"
    Sfx.play("win")
    status_label.text = "All jellyfish saved! Level complete."
    Game.level_complete()

func _lose():
    state = "over"
    Sfx.play("lose")
    status_label.text = "The sun rose... Press Enter to restart"

func resolve_blocked_position(pos: Vector2) -> Vector2:
    var margin = 1  # small push to avoid constant crossing
    for rect in rock_rects:
        if rect.has_point(pos):
            var left = pos.x - rect.position.x
            var right = rect.end.x - pos.x
            var top = pos.y - rect.position.y
            var bottom = rect.end.y - pos.y
            var min_dist = min(min(left, right), min(top, bottom))
            if min_dist == left:

            elif min_dist == right:
                pos.x = rect.end.x + margin
            elif min_dist == top:
                pos.y = rect.position.y - margin
            else:
                pos.y = rect.end.y + margin
    return pos

# Helper: keep a point inside the viewport, respecting radius
func clamp_to_viewport(pos: Vector2, radius: float) -> Vector2:
    pos.x = clamp(pos.x, radius, VIEWPORT_SIZE.x - radius)
    pos.y = clamp(pos.y, radius, VIEWPORT_SIZE.y - radius)
    return pos

# Helper: push a circle away from circular obstacles
func resolve_circle_collisions(pos: Vector2, radius: float, centers: Array, obs_radius: float) -> Vector2:
    for center in centers:
        var diff = pos - center
        var dist = diff.length()
        var min_dist = radius + obs_radius
        if dist < min_dist and dist > 0.0:
            var push = diff.normalized() * (min_dist - dist)
            pos += push
    return pos

    add_child(tide_pool_area)

    # Obstacle rocks
    var rock_positions = [

func _process(delta):
    if state == "title":
        label.text = "Last Gleam Before Dawn - Press Enter to start"
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            state = "playing"
        return
    if state == "over":
        if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
            get_tree().reload_current_scene()
        return
    if state == "won":
        return

    sun_time_left -= delta
    if sun_time_left <= 0.0:
        sun_time_left = 0.0
        if settled_count < jellyfishes.size():
            state = "over"
            Sfx.play("lose")
            label.text = "The sun has risen... some jellyfish left stranded. Press Enter to restart"
        else:
            _win()
        return

    # Player movement with rock collision
    var vel = Vector2.ZERO
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"):
        vel.x += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
        vel.x -= 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):
        vel.y += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
        vel.y -= 1

    var new_y = player.position.y
    if not _point_collides_with_rocks(Vector2(new_x, new_y)):

    new_y = player.position.y + vel.y

    # Clamp inside viewport (keep player fully visible)
    new_pos.x = clamp(new_pos.x, 64.0, 960.0)
    new_pos.y = clamp(new_pos.y, 64.0, 512.0)
    player.position = new_pos

    for j in jellyfishes:
        if j["settled"]:
            Anim.hover(j["sprite"])
            continue
        var j_pos = j["area"].position
        var dist = j_pos.distance_to(player.position)
        if dist < panic_radius and dist > 0.01:
            var flee_dir = (j_pos - player.position).normalized()
            var flee_move = flee_dir * flee_speed * delta
            var target_pos = j_pos + flee_move
            # Attempt full move, then try sliding
            if not _point_collides_with_rocks(target_pos):
                j_pos = target_pos
            else:
                var try_x = Vector2(j_pos.x + flee_move.x, j_pos.y)
                if not _point_collides_with_rocks(try_x):
                    j_pos = try_x
                else:
                    var try_y = Vector2(j_pos.x, j_pos.y + flee_move.y)
                    if not _point_collides_with_rocks(try_y):
                        j_pos = try_y

        # Keep jellyfish visible
        j_pos.x = clamp(j_pos.x, 64.0, 960.0)
        j_pos.y = clamp(j_pos.y, 64.0, 512.0)
        j["area"].position = j_pos
        Anim.hover(j["sprite"])

    # Player animation
    var is_moving = vel.length_squared() > 0.0
    Anim.walk(player_sprite, is_moving, vel.x if is_moving else 0.0)

    # Update UI
    var time_display = int(ceil(sun_time_left))
    label.text = "Jellyfish: %d/%d  Sunrise in: %d" % [settled_count, jellyfishes.size(), time_display]

func _point_collides_with_rocks(point: Vector2) -> bool:
    for rect in rock_rects:
        if rect.has_point(point):
            return true
    return false

    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):

    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):

    for i in range(num_jacks):

        jack.position = jack_positions[i]

        var shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
        var circle = CircleShape2D.new()
        circle.radius = 50.0
        shape.shape = circle
        jack.add_child(shape)
        jack.area_entered.connect(_on_jack_area_entered)
        add_child(jack)
        jacks.append(jack)
        claimed.append(false)

    # ghost
    ghost = Area2D.new()
    ghost.position = waypoints[0]
    ghost.set_meta("ghost", true)
    ghost_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
    ghost_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_blizzard_ghost_00001_.png")

func _on_player_area_entered(area: Area2D):
    if state != "playing":
        return
    if area.get_meta("ghost", false):
        state = "over"
        Sfx.play("lose")
        status_label.text = "Frozen by the blizzard! Press Enter to restart"
        return
    if area.has_meta("jack_index"):
        var idx = area.get_meta("jack_index")
        if idx == current_target:
            claimed[idx] = true
            jack_sprites[idx].modulate = Color.GREEN
            # advance to next unclaimed jack
            current_target = _next_unclaimed(idx)
            if current_target == num_jacks and not has_won:
                has_won = true
                state = "won"
                Sfx.play("win")
                status_label.text = "All lines reconnected – level complete!"
                Game.level_complete()

func _on_jack_area_entered(area: Area2D):
    # jacks detecting ghost handled by ghost's own area_entered
    pass

func _on_ghost_area_entered(area: Area2D):
    if state != "playing":
        return
    if area.has_meta("jack_index"):
        var idx = area.get_meta("jack_index")
        if claimed[idx]:
            claimed[idx] = false
            jack_sprites[idx].modulate = Color.WHITE
            if idx < current_target:
                current_target = idx
            # ensure current_target points to the earliest unclaimed
            current_target = _next_unclaimed(-1)

func _next_unclaimed(start: int) -> int:
    for i in range(start + 1, num_jacks):
        if not claimed[i]:
            return i
    # also check if some earlier jack was unclaimed after being claimed
    for i in range(0, start + 1):
        if not claimed[i]:
            return i
    return num_jacks

func _process(delta):

        return

        velocity.x += 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
        velocity.x -= 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):
        velocity.y += 1.0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
        velocity.y -= 1.0
    player.position += velocity.normalized() * player_speed * delta
    player.position = player.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))

    # player animation
    var moving = velocity.length() > 0
    var dir_x = velocity.normalized().x if moving else 0.0
    Anim.walk(player_sprite, moving, dir_x)

    # ghost patrol
    var target = waypoints[current_waypoint]
    var dir = target - ghost.position
    var dist = dir.length()
    if dist < 5.0:
        current_waypoint = (current_waypoint + 1) % waypoints.size()
    else:
        ghost.position += dir.normalized() * ghost_speed * delta
    Anim.hover(ghost_sprite)

    # label
    var connected = 0
    for c in claimed:
        if c:
            connected += 1
    if current_target < num_jacks:
        status_label.text = "Connect jack %d - Lines: %d/%d" % [current_target + 1, connected, num_jacks]
    else:
        status_label.text = "All jacks connected! %d/%d" % [connected, num_jacks]

# Push a position out of a circular obstacle
func push_out_of_circle(pos: Vector2, center: Vector2, radius: float, own_radius: float) -> Vector2:
	var to = pos - center
	var dist = to.length()
	var min_dist = radius + own_radius
	if dist < min_dist and dist > 0.001:
		return center + to.normalized() * min_dist
	return pos

# Scale a sprite so its longest axis fits DESIRED pixels
func fit_sprite(sprite: Sprite2D, desired: float) -> void:
	var tex = sprite.texture
	if tex == null:
		return
	var s = desired / max(tex.get_width(), tex.get_height())
	sprite.scale = Vector2(s, s)

	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"): move_input.x += 1
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):  move_input.x -= 1
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):  move_input.y += 1
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):    move_input.y -= 1

			Anim.hover(jelly["sprite"])

		var prev_pos = j_pos
		var dist = j_pos.distance_to(player.position)

		if dist < panic_radius:

					break
			if blocked:
				j_area.position = prev_pos
		else:
			var seed = jelly["drift_seed"]
			var drift_x = sin(elapsed * 3.7 + seed) * 18.0 * delta
			var drift_y = cos(elapsed * 2.9 + seed + 1.3) * 18.0 * delta
			var new_pos = j_pos + Vector2(drift_x, drift_y)
			new_pos = new_pos.clamp(Vector2(8, 8), Vector2(1016, 568))
			j_area.position = new_pos
			var blocked = false
			for rock in rocks:
				if j_area.overlaps_area(rock):
					blocked = true
					break
			if blocked:
				j_area.position = prev_pos

		Anim.hover(jelly["sprite"])

	var t = int(ceil(time_remaining))
	var color_hint = ""
	if t <= 10:
		color_hint = "  ⚠ DAWN!"
	status_label.text = "Time: %d s%s   Saved: %d/%d" % [t, color_hint, settled_count, num_jellyfish]

func _win():

		return
	state = "won"
	Sfx.play("win")
	status_label.text = "All jellyfish safe! The sea claims them back.\nLevel complete!"
	Game.level_complete()

func _unlock_door():
    # Remove locked door visual and collision rect

        locked_door_sprite.queue_free()
        locked_door_sprite = null
    # Remove its rect from active walls (the one we added)
    for i in range(active_wall_rects.size() - 1, -1, -1):
        var r: Rect2 = active_wall_rects[i]
        if r.position.x == 600 and r.position.y == 200 and r.size == Vector2(24, 176):

        Anim.flash(player_sprite)

            Sfx.play("lose")
            status_label.text = "Caught by the clockwork cat... Press Enter to restart"

func _hits_wall(pos: Vector2) -> bool:
    var half = Vector2(player_half, player_half)
    var player_rect = Rect2(pos - half, half * 2.0)
    for w in active_wall_rects:
        if player_rect.intersects(w):
            return true
    return false

        hit_cooldown -= delta

    var patroller_motion = patroller.position.direction_to(target) * patroller_speed * delta
    patroller.position = patroller.position.move_toward(target, patroller_speed * delta)
    if patroller.position.distance_to(target) < 2.0:
        patroller_index = (patroller_index + 1) % patrol_points.size()
    var patroller_dir = (target - patroller.position).normalized().x

    # Animate patroller
    Anim.walk(patroller_sprite, true, patroller_dir)

    # Player input
    var input_dir = Vector2(
        Input.get_action_strength("ui_right") - Input.get_action_strength("ui_left"),
        Input.get_action_strength("ui_down") - Input.get_action_strength("ui_up")
    ).normalized()
    var is_moving = input_dir.length() > 0
    var motion = input_dir * player_speed * delta

    # Axis‑separated collision
    var new_x = player.position + Vector2(motion.x, 0)

    var new_y = player.position + Vector2(0, motion.y)

    # Player animation
    Anim.walk(player_sprite, is_moving, input_dir.x)

    # UI update
    status_label.text = "Gems: %d / %d   Lives: %d" % [score, total_gems, lives]

			state = "over"

		await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout
		player.monitoring = true

func _hits_wall(pos: Vector2) -> bool:
	var half = Vector2(player_half_size, player_half_size)
	var player_rect = Rect2(pos - half, half * 2)
	for w in walls:
		if player_rect.intersects(w):
			return true
	return false

func _process(delta):

	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):

	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):

extends Node2D

@export var speed = 240.0
var panic_radius = 130.0
var flee_speed = 90.0
var goal_radius = 72.0
var number_of_bees = 5

var state = "title"
var player: Area2D
var player_sprite: Sprite2D
var creatures: Array[Area2D] = []
var creature_sprites: Array[Sprite2D] = []
var creature_settled: Array[bool] = []
var goal: Area2D
var goal_sprite: Sprite2D
var goal_circle: CircleShape2D
var status_label: Label
var settled_count = 0

func _ready():
	var background = Sprite2D.new()
	background.texture = load("res://assets/level_0_bg.png")
	background.centered = false
	background.position = Vector2.ZERO
	background.z_index = -1
	add_child(background)

	player = Area2D.new()
	player.position = Vector2(100, 300)
	player_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	player_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/hero_sprite.png")
	player.add_child(player_sprite)
	var player_shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
	var player_circle = CircleShape2D.new()
	player_circle.radius = 20.0
	player_shape.shape = player_circle
	player.add_child(player_shape)
	add_child(player)
	Anim.set_poses(player_sprite, load("res://assets/hero_sprite.png"), load("res://assets/hero_walk.png"))

	goal = Area2D.new()
	goal.position = Vector2(920, 200)
	goal_sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	goal_sprite.texture = load("res://assets/extra_brass_hive.png")
	goal_sprite.scale = Vector2(1.0, 1.0)
	goal.add_child(goal_sprite)
	var goal_shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
	goal_circle = CircleShape2D.new()
	goal_circle.radius = goal_radius
	goal_shape.shape = goal_circle
	goal.add_child(goal_shape)
	add_child(goal)

	for pos in [Vector2(180, 480), Vector2(750, 90), Vector2(400, 250)]:
		var rock = Sprite2D.new()
		rock.texture = load("res://assets/extra_meadow_rock.png")
		rock.position = pos
		rock.z_index = 0
		add_child(rock)

	var bee_positions = [Vector2(220, 180), Vector2(310, 460), Vector2(520, 140), Vector2(610, 400), Vector2(700, 250)]
	for pos in bee_positions:
		_spawn_bee(pos)

	var canvas = CanvasLayer.new()
	add_child(canvas)
	status_label = Label.new()
	status_label.position = Vector2(20, 20)
	status_label.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 22)
	canvas.add_child(status_label)

	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless" or Game.level > 0:
		state = "playing"

func _spawn_bee(pos: Vector2):
	var creature = Area2D.new()
	creature.position = pos
	var sprite = Sprite2D.new()
	sprite.texture = load("res://assets/key_item.png")
	sprite.scale = Vector2(0.65, 0.65)
	creature.add_child(sprite)
	var shape = CollisionShape2D.new()
	var circle = CircleShape2D.new()
	circle.radius = 22.0
	shape.shape = circle
	creature.add_child(shape)
	add_child(creature)
	creatures.append(creature)
	creature_sprites.append(sprite)
	creature_settled.append(false)

func _process(delta):
	if state == "title":
		status_label.text = "CLOCKWORK VESPERS - Press Enter to start"
		if Input.is_action_just_pressed("ui_accept"):
			state = "playing"
		return
	if state == "won":
		return

	var move_vec = Vector2.ZERO
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"):
		move_vec.x += 1
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
		move_vec.x -= 1
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_down"):
		move_vec.y += 1
	if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
		move_vec.y -= 1
	var direction = move_vec.normalized()
	var is_moving = move_vec.length() > 0.0
	player.position += direction * speed * delta
	player.position = player.position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, Vector2(1024, 576))
	Anim.walk(player_sprite, is_moving, direction.x)

	for i in creatures.size():
		var creature = creatures[i]
		if creature_settled[i]:
			Anim.hover(creature_sprites[i])
			continue
		if creature.global_position.distance_to(goal.global_position) <= goal_radius:
			_settle_bee(i)
			continue
		var dist = creature.global_position.distance_to(player.global_position)
		if dist < panic_radius:
			var flee_dir = (creature.global_position - player.global_position).normalized()
			creature.position += flee_dir * flee_speed * delta
			creature.position = creature.position.clamp(Vector2(24, 24), Vector2(1000, 552))
			creature_sprites[i].scale.x = abs(creature_sprites[i].scale.x) if flee_dir.x >= 0 else -abs(creature_sprites[i].scale.x)
			Anim.hover(creature_sprites[i])
		else:
			Anim.hover(creature_sprites[i])

	if settled_count == number_of_bees:
		state = "won"
		Sfx.play("win")
		status_label.text = "All bees are home! Level complete."
		Game.level_complete()
		return

	status_label.text = "Bees herded: %d/%d" % [settled_count, number_of_bees]

func _settle_bee(i: int):
	creature_settled[i] = true
	Sfx.play("pickup")
	var tween = create_tween()
	tween.tween_property(creature_sprites[i], "global_position", goal.global_position, 0.4)
	tween.parallel().tween_property(creature_sprites[i], "modulate:a", 0.0, 0.4)
	tween.tween_callback(func(): creature_sprites[i].visible = false)
	settled_count += 1

## Engine reference (background knowledge)

Vendored Godot/game-design references for this system. They describe general Godot 4 practice, not SAGA's output contract - where they disagree with the rules that follow, the rules that follow win.

### Reference: godot-2d-movement

# Godot 2D Movement (4.x)

Build responsive 2D character controllers with `CharacterBody2D` and the argument-less
`move_and_slide()`. Targets **Godot 4.3+**.

## When to use

- Use when scripting a 2D player/enemy that moves and collides: platformer (gravity +
  jump) or top-down (free 8-direction), slope walking, or wall/floor detection.
- Use when `move_and_slide()` "does nothing", the character sinks through floors, or
  `is_on_floor()` is always false.

**When *not* to use:** dynamic rigid bodies, areas, raycasts, collision layers →
`godot-physics`; tile-based levels → `godot-tilemap`; full platformer game template →
the `platformer` genre skill; engine-agnostic feel tuning → `physics-tuning`.

## Core workflow

1. **Use `CharacterBody2D`** with a `CollisionShape2D` child. It is script-driven: it
   does not fall or react to forces on its own.
2. **Set the `velocity` property, then call `move_and_slide()`** (no arguments in 4.x).
   The method reads `velocity`, moves the body, slides along surfaces, and updates
   `velocity` to reflect what actually happened.
3. **Do it in `_physics_process(delta)`** — `move_and_slide()` uses the physics step's
   delta internally, so do not multiply `velocity` by `delta` yourself.
4. **Platformer:** add gravity to `velocity.y` each tick, jump by setting `velocity.y`
   negative when `is_on_floor()`.
5. **Top-down:** build a direction from input and scale by speed; set
   `motion_mode = MOTION_MODE_FLOATING` so there is no "floor/wall" distinction.
6. **Read results** with `is_on_floor()`, `is_on_wall()`, `get_wall_normal()`, and
   `get_slide_collision(i)` after the call.

## Patterns

### 1. Platformer controller (gravity, jump, slopes)

```gdscript
extends CharacterBody2D

@export var speed := 200.0
@export var jump_velocity := -400.0
@export var gravity := 1200.0          # pixels/sec^2 (tune to taste)

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    # Apply gravity while airborne.
    if not is_on_floor():
        velocity.y += gravity * delta

    # Jump only when grounded (Input action set in Project Settings > Input Map).
    if Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump") and is_on_floor():
        velocity.y = jump_velocity

    # Horizontal input: -1, 0, or 1.
    var dir := Input.get_axis("move_left", "move_right")
    if dir != 0.0:
        velocity.x = dir * speed
    else:
        velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, 0.0, speed)   # decelerate to a stop

    move_and_slide()   # 4.x: no arguments; uses and updates `velocity`
```

### 2. Top-down 8-direction movement

```gdscript
extends CharacterBody2D

@export var speed := 220.0

func _ready() -> void:
    motion_mode = CharacterBody2D.MOTION_MODE_FLOATING  # no floor/ceiling concept

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
    # get_vector returns a normalized-ish Vector2 from four input actions.
    var input := Input.get_vector("move_left", "move_right", "move_up", "move_down")
    velocity = input * speed
    move_and_slide()
```

### 3. Reading slide collisions after moving

```gdscript
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    # ... set velocity ...
    move_and_slide()
    for i in get_slide_collision_count():
        var c := get_slide_collision(i)
        var other := c.get_collider()
        if other and other.is_in_group("enemies"):
            take_damage(1)        # touched an enemy while moving
```

### 4. Coyote time (forgiving jump just after leaving a ledge)

```gdscript
@export var coyote_time := 0.1
var _coyote := 0.0

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    if not is_on_floor():
        velocity.y += gravity * delta
        _coyote -= delta
    else:
        _coyote = coyote_time

    if Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump") and _coyote > 0.0:
        velocity.y = jump_velocity
        _coyote = 0.0
    # ... horizontal input + move_and_slide() ...
```

## Pitfalls

- **3.x signature is gone.** `move_and_slide(velocity)` (returning the new velocity) was
  removed. In 4.x set the `velocity` property and call `move_and_slide()` with no args.
  `move_and_slide(velocity, Vector2.UP)` will not parse.
- **Multiplying velocity by delta.** `move_and_slide()` already accounts for the physics
  delta. Setting `velocity = dir * speed * delta` makes the body crawl.
- **Movement in `_process`** instead of `_physics_process` causes frame-rate-dependent,
  jittery motion. Always move in `_physics_process`.
- **`is_on_floor()` always false** when `up_direction` is wrong (default `Vector2.UP`),
  there is no `CollisionShape2D`, or you never called `move_and_slide()` this frame.
- **Sinking through floors** usually means the collision shape is missing/zero-sized, the
  floor body is on a layer this body's mask doesn't include, or you moved the body via
  `position +=` instead of velocity + `move_and_slide()`.
- **Slope slipping while idle:** keep `floor_stop_on_slope = true` (default) and set a
  `floor_snap_length` so the body sticks to downward slopes.

## References

- For one-way platforms, moving platforms, jump buffering, variable jump height, and
  `move_and_collide()` (manual collision response), read `references/controller-recipes.md`.

## Related skills

- `godot-physics` — collision layers/masks, areas, raycasts, rigid bodies.
- `godot-tilemap` — building the levels this character walks on.
- `godot-animation` — driving sprite/skeletal animation from movement state.
- `camera-systems` — follow camera, deadzone, and look-ahead that track this character.
- `platformer` / `input-systems` — full genre template and rebindable input.

### Reference: godot-ui-control

# Godot UI / Control nodes (4.x)

Lay out responsive UI with `Control` anchors and `Container` nodes, style it with a
`Theme`, and make it navigable by keyboard and gamepad. Targets **Godot 4.3+**.

## When to use

- Use when building HUDs, menus, inventories, dialog boxes, or settings screens with
  `Control`-derived nodes; arranging UI that adapts to window size; theming; or wiring
  focus navigation for controller/keyboard.

**When *not* to use:** in-world 2D nodes (`Node2D`/sprites) → `godot-nodes-scenes`;
animating UI transitions → `godot-animation` (Tween); genre UIs like card hands →
`card-game`/`visual-novel`. For full input rebinding → `input-systems`.

## Core workflow

1. **Use `Control` nodes for UI**, not `Node2D`. Controls have a rect (position + size),
   anchors, and participate in focus/theming.
2. **Anchor for responsiveness.** Anchors are fractions (0–1) of the parent rect that the
   Control's edges stick to. Use the editor's **Layout** presets (Top-Left, Full Rect,
   Center, etc.) instead of hand-placing pixels.
3. **Let Containers position children.** Put children in a `VBoxContainer`,
   `HBoxContainer`, `GridContainer`, `MarginContainer`, etc. — the container sets their
   position/size; you control flow with `size_flags`. Don't set child anchors inside a
   container (it overrides them).
4. **Style with a `Theme`.** Assign a `Theme` resource on a top Control; children inherit
   it. Override per-node with theme overrides only when necessary.
5. **Wire focus** so gamepad/keyboard can move between buttons; set a default focused
   control and define neighbors or rely on auto-neighbor.
6. **Connect signals** (`pressed`, `toggled`, `text_submitted`, `value_changed`).

## Patterns

### 1. Responsive layout with anchors (code form)

```gdscript
extends Control

func _ready() -> void:
    # Stretch this panel to fill its parent (equivalent to the "Full Rect" preset).
    anchors_preset = Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT
    # Or set anchors manually: all four edges at the parent's far corners.
    # anchor_left = 0; anchor_top = 0; anchor_right = 1; anchor_bottom = 1
```

### 2. A menu built from containers + button signals

```gdscript
extends VBoxContainer    # children stack vertically, auto-sized

func _ready() -> void:
    for child in get_children():
        if child is Button:
            child.pressed.connect(_on_button_pressed.bind(child.name))
    # Give the first button focus so a gamepad can navigate immediately.
    if get_child_count() > 0:
        (get_child(0) as Control).grab_focus()

func _on_button_pressed(which: StringName) -> void:
    match which:
        "PlayButton":  get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://game.tscn")
        "QuitButton":  get_tree().quit()
```

### 3. Size flags: make one child expand to fill leftover space

```gdscript
# In a HBoxContainer: a label on the left, a spacer that eats remaining width.
func _ready() -> void:
    $Label.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_BEGIN
    $Spacer.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL   # grows to fill
```

### 4. Theme override for one node (without a full Theme resource)

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
    # Per-node overrides: use add_theme_* (type-specific setters).
    $Title.add_theme_font_size_override("font_size", 32)
    $Title.add_theme_color_override("font_color", Color.GOLD)
    $Panel.add_theme_stylebox_override("panel", preload("res://ui/panel.stylebox.tres"))
```

## Pitfalls

- **Mixing manual position with Containers.** A child of a `Container` cannot set its own
  position/anchors — the container owns layout. To free-place, take the node out of the
  container or use a plain `Control`/`PanelContainer` wrapper.
- **Anchors vs offsets.** Anchors are fractions of the parent; offsets are pixel deltas
  from the anchored point. Set anchors via presets, then nudge with offsets. Setting only
  position while anchors are at 0 makes UI not scale with the window.
- **`Node2D` for UI.** Buttons/labels parented under a `Node2D` won't theme or take focus
  correctly. Keep UI under a `CanvasLayer`/`Control` subtree.
- **Focus lost on gamepad.** If nothing is focused, directional input does nothing. Call
  `grab_focus()` on an initial control and ensure `focus_mode` is not `FOCUS_NONE`.
- **Theme vs theme override.** A `Theme` resource styles a whole subtree; `add_theme_*`
  overrides one node. Overusing per-node overrides defeats centralized theming.
- **`rect_*` properties are renamed.** Godot 3's `rect_size`/`rect_position`/`rect_min_size`
  are now `size`/`position`/`custom_minimum_size` in 4.x.
- **`mouse_filter`** on a full-rect Control can swallow clicks meant for nodes beneath it;
  set `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` on purely decorative panels.

# Godot Physics (4.x, 2D + 3D)

Pick the right physics body, wire up collision layers/masks, detect overlaps, and cast
rays. Concepts apply to both 2D and 3D (swap the `2D`/`3D` suffix). Targets
**Godot 4.3+**.

## When to use

- Use when choosing between body types, setting collision layers/masks so the right
  things collide, detecting overlaps (triggers, hurtboxes) with `Area`, applying
  forces/impulses to a `RigidBody`, or casting rays for line-of-sight/ground checks.

**When *not* to use:** kinematic character controllers (`move_and_slide`) →
`godot-2d-movement`; tile collision setup → `godot-tilemap`; tuning the *feel* of physics
(timestep, mass, jitter) → `physics-tuning`.

## Core workflow

1. **Choose the body type:**
   - `StaticBody` — never moves (floors, walls). Collides, no simulation.
   - `RigidBody` — fully simulated (gravity, forces, bouncing). Don't set its
     `position` directly; apply forces/impulses or set `linear_velocity`.
   - `CharacterBody` — script-driven kinematic (see `godot-2d-movement`).
   - `Area` — detects overlaps and can apply gravity/damping; no solid collision.
   Every body needs a `CollisionShape` (or `CollisionPolygon`) child.
2. **Configure layers and masks.** A body is *on* its **layers** and *scans for* its
   **masks**. Two bodies interact only if one's layer is in the other's mask. Name layers
   in Project Settings > Layer Names for clarity.
3. **Detect overlaps** with `Area` signals (`body_entered`, `area_entered`).
4. **Drive RigidBodies with forces/impulses**, or override `_integrate_forces` for full
   control.
5. **Cast rays** with a `RayCast2D/3D` node (polled each frame) or a one-shot space-state
   query from code.

## Patterns

### 1. Collision layers vs masks (set from code)

```gdscript
# Player is on layer 1, scans layers 2 (walls) and 3 (enemies).
func _ready() -> void:
    set_collision_layer_value(1, true)    # I am on layer 1
    set_collision_mask_value(2, true)     # I collide with things on layer 2
    set_collision_mask_value(3, true)     # ...and layer 3
    # Bit-field forms also exist: collision_layer = 1; collision_mask = 0b110
```

### 2. Area2D as a trigger / hurtbox

```gdscript
extends Area2D                            # e.g. a damage zone

func _ready() -> void:
    body_entered.connect(_on_body_entered)
    area_entered.connect(_on_area_entered)

func _on_body_entered(body: Node2D) -> void:
    if body.has_method("take_damage"):
        body.take_damage(10)

func _on_area_entered(area: Area2D) -> void:
    print("Overlapped area: ", area.name)
```

### 3. Applying force and impulse to a RigidBody3D

```gdscript
extends RigidBody3D

func push(direction: Vector3) -> void:
    apply_central_impulse(direction * 8.0)     # instantaneous velocity change

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
    apply_central_force(Vector3.FORWARD * 4.0) # continuous force (per tick)
    # Never set `position` on a RigidBody to move it; use forces/impulses or
    # set linear_velocity. Use freeze=true if you must hold it in place.
```

### 4. Raycast two ways

```gdscript
# A) RayCast2D node: enable it, then poll after physics has updated.
@onready var ray: RayCast2D = $RayCast2D    # set target_position in the editor

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
    if ray.is_colliding():
        var hit := ray.get_collider()
        var point := ray.get_collision_point()

# B) One-shot query from code (no node needed).
func ground_under(global_from: Vector2) -> Dictionary:
    var space := get_world_2d().direct_space_state
    var query := PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D.create(global_from, global_from + Vector2(0, 64))
    query.collision_mask = 1                 # only layer 1
    return space.intersect_ray(query)        # {} if nothing hit, else collider/position/normal
```

## Pitfalls

- **Layer vs mask confusion** is the #1 bug. Layer = "what I am"; mask = "what I look
  for". For A to detect B, B's layer must be in A's mask. Detection can be one-directional.
- **Moving a RigidBody by `position`** fights the solver and causes tunneling/jitter.
  Use impulses/forces, set `linear_velocity`, or `freeze` it. To teleport, set position
  and zero the velocities inside `_integrate_forces`.
- **`Area` doesn't fire** when neither monitoring nor monitorable is set, or layers/masks
  don't overlap. `monitoring` must be on for the Area to detect; `monitorable` lets others
  detect it.
- **RayCast2D/3D read stale or no data** if `enabled` is false, or if you read it before
  physics updated — read in `_physics_process`, and call `force_raycast_update()` after
  moving it within the same tick.
- **Forgetting a `CollisionShape`** (or leaving it empty) means the body never collides.
- **Fast objects tunnel** through thin walls; enable **continuous CD** on the RigidBody
  (`continuous_cd`) or use a raycast-based check.
- **`intersect_ray` excludes its own body?** Pass `query.exclude = [self.get_rid()]` (an
  `Array[RID]`, not an array of nodes) to skip self-hits.

  shape queries (`intersect_shape`), and 3D `move_and_collide`, read

# Game AI: decisions, steering, and pathfinding

Build believable NPC behavior from three separable layers: **decide** (what to
do), **steer** (how to move there), and **path** (how to route around the map).
Keep them decoupled — a behavior tree picks a target, the pathfinder produces
waypoints, steering follows them. This skill teaches the engine-neutral
algorithms; bind them to your engine via the related skills below.

## When to use

- Use when implementing enemy/NPC logic: patrols, chase/flee, guard states,
  group movement, or "find a path to the player".
- Use to choose between an **FSM** (few clear states), a **behavior tree** (many
  reactive behaviors with priorities), or **steering** (smooth local movement).
- Use when integrating pathfinding: A* on a grid/graph, or driving an engine
  navmesh agent.

**When *not* to use:** for the engine's concrete navmesh/agent API and baking,
use `unity-navmesh`, `unreal-behavior-trees`, or Godot's `NavigationAgent2D/3D`
(see that engine skill). For movement/collision feel, use `physics-tuning`. For
spawning waves along lanes, see the `tower-defense` genre skill.

## Core workflow

1. **Pick the decision model by complexity.** 2–5 states with obvious
   transitions → FSM. Many behaviors, priorities, interruption, reuse → behavior
   tree. Continuous "how strongly do I want each option" → utility scoring.
2. **Separate decision from motion.** The decision layer outputs an *intent*
   (target position, action). Steering or pathfinding turns intent into motion.
3. **Path on the right graph.** Grid tiles, waypoint graph, or a baked navmesh.
   Fewer nodes = faster A*. Prefer the engine's navmesh for 3D; A* on a grid for
   tile games.
4. **Steer along the path**, not straight to the goal — follow the next waypoint,
   advancing when close, so agents round corners.
5. **Recompute paths sparingly.** Pathfind on a timer or when the goal moves a
   tile, not every frame. Cache the path; only the waypoint index advances.
6. **Verify by observation.** Watch the agent: does it reach the goal, get stuck
   on corners, oscillate between states? Draw the path and current state on
   screen while tuning.

## Patterns

### 1. Finite state machine (one state object, explicit transitions)

```gdscript
# Each state is a small object with enter/update/exit. The machine owns "current".
class_name State
func enter(agent): pass
func update(agent, dt) -> State: return null   # return a new state to transition
func exit(agent): pass

# --- Chase state: returns Patrol when the player escapes sight range ---
class Chase extends State:
    func update(agent, dt) -> State:
        if not agent.can_see(agent.target):
            return Patrol.new()                 # transition by returning next state
        agent.move_toward(agent.target.position, dt)
        return null                             # null = stay in this state

# --- Driver: call once per frame ---
func tick(dt):
    var next = current.update(self, dt)
    if next != null:
        current.exit(self); next.enter(self); current = next
```

Keep transition logic *inside* states (or in a table), never as a growing pile
of `if` flags. One state owns one behavior; that is what keeps an FSM readable.

### 2. Behavior tree tick (composite nodes return a status)

```gdscript
# A node's tick() returns SUCCESS, FAILURE, or RUNNING (still working this frame).
enum Status { SUCCESS, FAILURE, RUNNING }

# Sequence: run children in order; stop at the first non-SUCCESS (logical AND).
func sequence_tick(children, agent, dt) -> int:
    for child in children:
        var s = child.tick(agent, dt)
        if s != Status.SUCCESS:
            return s                 # FAILURE or RUNNING short-circuits the sequence
    return Status.SUCCESS

# Selector: try children until one succeeds or is RUNNING (logical OR / fallback).
func selector_tick(children, agent, dt) -> int:
    for child in children:
        var s = child.tick(agent, dt)
        if s != Status.FAILURE:
            return s                 # SUCCESS or RUNNING stops the search
    return Status.FAILURE
```

A guard AI reads top-down: `Selector[ Sequence[CanSeePlayer?, Chase], Patrol ]`
— chase if visible, otherwise patrol. See `references/behavior-trees.md` for
leaf nodes, decorators (Inverter, Cooldown), and a blackboard.

### 3. Steering: seek and arrive (smooth, frame-rate independent)

```gdscript
# Seek: accelerate toward a target at full speed. Steering = desired - current.
func seek(pos, vel, target, max_speed, max_force) -> Vector2:
    var desired = (target - pos).normalized() * max_speed
    return (desired - vel).limit_length(max_force)   # a force, not a teleport

# Arrive: like seek, but ramp speed down inside slow_radius so it stops cleanly.
func arrive(pos, vel, target, max_speed, max_force, slow_radius) -> Vector2:
    var offset = target - pos
    var dist = offset.length()
    if dist < 0.001: return -vel                      # already there: kill drift
    var ramped = max_speed * min(dist / slow_radius, 1.0)
    var desired = offset / dist * ramped
    return (desired - vel).limit_length(max_force)

# Per frame: vel += steering * dt; pos += vel * dt   (always scale by dt)
```

### 4. A* heuristic must not overestimate (or paths stop being shortest)

```python
# Match the heuristic to the movement. An ADMISSIBLE heuristic (never larger
# than the true remaining cost) keeps A* optimal.
def heuristic(a, b):
    dx, dy = abs(a.x - b.x), abs(a.y - b.y)
    # return dx + dy             # Manhattan: 4-direction grids (no diagonals)
    return (dx + dy) + (1.414 - 2) * min(dx, dy)   # octile: 8-direction grids
# f(n) = g(n) + h(n): g = cost from start, h = heuristic to goal.
# Overestimating h is faster but no longer guarantees the shortest path.
```

The full A* loop (priority queue, `came_from` reconstruction, grid + waypoint
graphs) is in `references/pathfinding.md`.

## Pitfalls

- **Pathfinding every frame** tanks the frame rate. Recompute on a timer or only
  when the target moves to a new tile; follow the cached waypoints in between.
- **Steering straight to the goal** instead of to the next waypoint makes agents
  hug walls and corners. Follow the path; advance the waypoint when within radius.
- **Inadmissible A\* heuristic** (e.g. Euclidean distance scaled up, or Manhattan
  on a diagonal grid) returns fast but *non-shortest* paths. Pick the heuristic
  that matches your allowed moves.
- **Behavior tree leaves that never return RUNNING** for multi-frame actions
  (walking, playing an animation) cause the tree to restart the action every
  tick. Return RUNNING until the action completes.
- **FSM transition spaghetti**: scattering `if state == ...` checks everywhere
  recreates the mess an FSM exists to prevent. Keep transitions in the state.
- **No line-of-sight or stuck check** → agents grind into walls forever. Add a
  timeout that forces a repath or a state change.

# Godot 2D Movement (4.x)

Build responsive 2D character controllers with `CharacterBody2D` and the argument-less
`move_and_slide()`. Targets **Godot 4.3+**.

## When to use

- Use when scripting a 2D player/enemy that moves and collides: platformer (gravity +
  jump) or top-down (free 8-direction), slope walking, or wall/floor detection.
- Use when `move_and_slide()` "does nothing", the character sinks through floors, or
  `is_on_floor()` is always false.

**When *not* to use:** dynamic rigid bodies, areas, raycasts, collision layers →
`godot-physics`; tile-based levels → `godot-tilemap`; full platformer game template →
the `platformer` genre skill; engine-agnostic feel tuning → `physics-tuning`.

## Core workflow

1. **Use `CharacterBody2D`** with a `CollisionShape2D` child. It is script-driven: it
   does not fall or react to forces on its own.
2. **Set the `velocity` property, then call `move_and_slide()`** (no arguments in 4.x).
   The method reads `velocity`, moves the body, slides along surfaces, and updates
   `velocity` to reflect what actually happened.
3. **Do it in `_physics_process(delta)`** — `move_and_slide()` uses the physics step's
   delta internally, so do not multiply `velocity` by `delta` yourself.
4. **Platformer:** add gravity to `velocity.y` each tick, jump by setting `velocity.y`
   negative when `is_on_floor()`.
5. **Top-down:** build a direction from input and scale by speed; set
   `motion_mode = MOTION_MODE_FLOATING` so there is no "floor/wall" distinction.
6. **Read results** with `is_on_floor()`, `is_on_wall()`, `get_wall_normal()`, and
   `get_slide_collision(i)` after the call.

## Patterns

### 1. Platformer controller (gravity, jump, slopes)

```gdscript
extends CharacterBody2D

@export var speed := 200.0
@export var jump_velocity := -400.0
@export var gravity := 1200.0          # pixels/sec^2 (tune to taste)

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    # Apply gravity while airborne.
    if not is_on_floor():
        velocity.y += gravity * delta

    # Jump only when grounded (Input action set in Project Settings > Input Map).
    if Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump") and is_on_floor():
        velocity.y = jump_velocity

    # Horizontal input: -1, 0, or 1.
    var dir := Input.get_axis("move_left", "move_right")
    if dir != 0.0:
        velocity.x = dir * speed
    else:
        velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, 0.0, speed)   # decelerate to a stop

    move_and_slide()   # 4.x: no arguments; uses and updates `velocity`
```

### 2. Top-down 8-direction movement

```gdscript
extends CharacterBody2D

@export var speed := 220.0

func _ready() -> void:
    motion_mode = CharacterBody2D.MOTION_MODE_FLOATING  # no floor/ceiling concept

func _physics_process(_delta: float) -> void:
    # get_vector returns a normalized-ish Vector2 from four input actions.
    var input := Input.get_vector("move_left", "move_right", "move_up", "move_down")
    velocity = input * speed
    move_and_slide()
```

### 3. Reading slide collisions after moving

```gdscript
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    # ... set velocity ...
    move_and_slide()
    for i in get_slide_collision_count():
        var c := get_slide_collision(i)
        var other := c.get_collider()
        if other and other.is_in_group("enemies"):
            take_damage(1)        # touched an enemy while moving
```

### 4. Coyote time (forgiving jump just after leaving a ledge)

```gdscript
@export var coyote_time := 0.1
var _coyote := 0.0

func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
    if not is_on_floor():
        velocity.y += gravity * delta
        _coyote -= delta
    else:
        _coyote = coyote_time

    if Input.is_action_just_pressed("jump") and _coyote > 0.0:
        velocity.y = jump_velocity
        _coyote = 0.0
    # ... horizontal input + move_and_slide() ...
```

## Pitfalls

- **3.x signature is gone.** `move_and_slide(velocity)` (returning the new velocity) was
  removed. In 4.x set the `velocity` property and call `move_and_slide()` with no args.
  `move_and_slide(velocity, Vector2.UP)` will not parse.
- **Multiplying velocity by delta.** `move_and_slide()` already accounts for the physics
  delta. Setting `velocity = dir * speed * delta` makes the body crawl.
- **Movement in `_process`** instead of `_physics_process` causes frame-rate-dependent,
  jittery motion. Always move in `_physics_process`.
- **`is_on_floor()` always false** when `up_direction` is wrong (default `Vector2.UP`),
  there is no `CollisionShape2D`, or you never called `move_and_slide()` this frame.
- **Sinking through floors** usually means the collision shape is missing/zero-sized, the
  floor body is on a layer this body's mask doesn't include, or you moved the body via
  `position +=` instead of velocity + `move_and_slide()`.
- **Slope slipping while idle:** keep `floor_stop_on_slope = true` (default) and set a
  `floor_snap_length` so the body sticks to downward slopes.

## References

  `move_and_collide()` (manual collision response), read `references/controller-recipes.md`.

- `camera-systems` — follow camera, deadzone, and look-ahead that track this character.
